label: Independent mean drift
interpretation: Mean relaxation creates a covariance footprint, so ESS often discards some early data, but it can stop before the retained-window mean is fully unbiased.

label: Independent variance relaxation
interpretation: This is the cleanest ESS failure mode: the samples are independent, so g is near one, but the marginal variance is still changing. MDTest sees this through its dispersion-trend screen.

label: Single metastable switch
interpretation: A sharp switch leaves a strong covariance footprint, so ESS can appear to detect the correct start. This is a real success on this case, but for an artifact-based reason.

label: Stationary underdamped AR(2)
interpretation: This process is stationary but oscillatory/correlated. ESS is the appropriate tool for the correlation penalty; stationarity screens should not over-truncate it.

label: Stationary AR(1)
interpretation: This is a stationary positive-correlation reference. The correct production start is zero; the useful quantity is the correlation penalty g, not equilibration truncation.

label: NarK volume
interpretation: Real MD example: no constructed true start; compare only MDTest and ESS recommendations.
